eligibility.evidence: Introduction, Results, and Materials and Methods: the study elicited moral advice from ChatGPT and experimentally tested its influence on participants’ judgments using trolley dilemmas.

paradigms.name: Trolley problem moral judgment: switch and bridge dilemmas
paradigms.source_paper: Foot (1967), Greene et al. (2001), and Thomson (1976)

D.population: US residents recruited through CloudResearch Prime Panels who correctly identified their advisor and the advice; mean age 39
D.metric: Proportion finding sacrifice of one life to save five morally acceptable

E.headline: ChatGPT gave inconsistent moral advice; in a separate experiment, its advice influenced participants’ moral judgments, even when identified as chatbot advice.

G.notes: The paper does not report the ChatGPT version, query date beyond the study’s December 21, 2022 data-collection date, or decoding settings. The authors analyze only the 41% who correctly identified both advisor and advice; a referee may ask about exclusions and generalizability.
